title: SE Project Requirements Schema
description: Single source of truth for requirements.yaml. CI uses this as the schema gate. Course-mandated fields: id / type / statement / fit_criterion / priority. Changes in this revision: (1) type is sub-typed into functional / invariant / quality / performance / cost / governance / security; (2) priority uses MoSCoW (must / should / could / wont) instead of P0-P2; (3) fit_criterion branching is per sub-type; (4) traceability, scope.modules, metric.baseline and source are removed (kept in trace-matrix.md / architecture blueprint / ADR instead); (5) priority_rationale added for delivery trade-offs only; (6) verification has minLength and metric names must be snake_case.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema itself. Bump it whenever fields change, so a CI result can be traced back to the rule set that produced it. Quote it in YAML, e.g. "1.0.0".

updated_at.description: YYYY-MM-DD, the date requirements.yaml was last modified.

notes.description: Optional. Change log for this revision, e.g. 'Aligned priorities with MoSCoW scope decision'.

requirements.description: Requirement list. Note: JSON Schema cannot check id uniqueness; that is enforced by validate_requirements.py instead.

requirement.description: A single requirement. Field order is recommended to match `required` for human readability.

id.description: Requirement ID, globally unique and never reused. Deprecate by changing status, never by deleting the number.

title.description: One-line title for trace-matrix and quick review.

type.description: Sub-typed requirement type. functional = observable behaviour; invariant = a rule that must never be violated under any applicable condition (detail stays in docs/architecture/invariants.md); quality / performance / cost / security = quantified non-functional constraints; governance = process / permission / approval rules that are executable or reviewable.

problem.description: What problem is being solved / what is wrong today. Without this an Agent cannot judge why a change is needed.

statement.description: Course-mandated field. The behaviour or constraint the system shall satisfy, written deterministically (shall / must not). Describes what, not how. For invariant types keep it short - the detailed rule lives in invariants.md.

owner.description: Primary owner's nickname, matching the division-of-labour table.

priority.description: MoSCoW prioritization. must = required for this delivery; should = important but deferrable if necessary; could = implement if time and resources allow; wont = explicitly out of scope for this version. MoSCoW fixes delivery scope, it does not encode urgency or build order - do not default everything to must.

priority_rationale.description: Optional but recommended for must / should. Records only the delivery trade-off behind the priority, e.g. why this is in scope now and what is being traded away. Full architecture trade-offs belong in an ADR, not here.

depends_on.description: Optional. IDs of requirements this one depends on.

safety_relevant.description: Whether this is a safety-relevant boundary: model output must not be trusted directly and needs deterministic code to constrain / check / fall back. The course requires at least one such boundary in the project.

status.description: draft -> approved (human confirmed) -> in_progress (Build) -> implemented -> verified (Test passed) -> deprecated.

version.description: Version of this requirement, e.g. 1 / 1.0 / v1.1. Bump whenever the content changes.

updated_at.description: YYYY-MM-DD, when this requirement was last modified.

notes.description: Optional. Change notes or open questions.

scope.description: Optional. What the change covers, expressed as behaviour-level boundaries. Concrete modules, file paths and write permissions are owned by the Architecture Blueprint, Structural Constraints and Permission Model - they are not repeated here.

in_scope.description: Optional. What this change will touch.

out_of_scope.description: Optional. What is explicitly not touched. Entries here double as evidence of Build's scope boundary.

fit_criterion.description: How far is 'done'. Course-mandated field and the only basis on which the Test Agent decides whether work is complete. Which child key is required depends on type: functional / governance -> checks; quality / performance / cost / security -> metrics; invariant -> at least one of them (metrics recommended).

summary.description: One-sentence definition of done, for humans.

checks.description: Acceptance points for functional / governance requirements (Given/When/Then or equivalent). Required when type is functional or governance.

metrics.description: Quantified metrics: metric + threshold + verification. Required when type is quality / performance / cost / security; recommended for invariant (zero-tolerance condition).

id.description: Acceptance point id, unique within its requirement.

verification.description: How to verify: offline test path::case name, a check command, or a link to a human review doc. Must not be empty.

automated.description: Whether CI can execute this automatically.

metric.description: The quantified triple: metric (what to measure) + threshold (how much is enough) + verification (where it is measured).

id.description: Metric id, unique within its requirement.

metric.description: Metric name, must be snake_case (lowercase letters, digits and underscores only), e.g. citation_resolution_success_rate.

unit.description: Optional. Unit: ratio / percent / seconds / USD / tokens / count. Must stay consistent with threshold (ratio -> 0.0-1.0, percent -> 0-100).

verification.description: How it is measured: test file::case name, an offline script, or a runtime monitor name. Must not be empty.
